Many of House (Hausu, 1977)'s most bizarre ideas came from the director's young daughter, who was asked a simple question: "What scares you?"

The result is one of the most imaginative horror films ever made. Directed by Nobuhiko Obayashi, House follows a group of schoolgirls who visit a countryside mansion where reality begins to break apart. Flying heads, carnivorous pianos, and haunted household objects turn the film into a surreal collision of horror, fantasy, comedy, and pure nightmare logic. Rather than aiming for realism, Obayashi embraced the boundless imagination of childhood, creating a film that remains unlike anything else nearly 50 years later.
